h1: Pullman Bangkok Hotel G — 5-Star Silom with a 10-Minute Walk to BNH Hospital
intro: Pullman Bangkok Hotel G is a 5-star Accor hotel at 188 Silom Road in the Bang Rak district of Bangkok. The building was constructed in 1992 and renovated in 2012, with 469 rooms spread across 38 floors, all with panoramic city views. Its place on the BNH Hospital shortlist comes from one specific fact: BNH Hospital (9/1 Convent Road) is roughly 800 metres away — about a 10-minute walk heading east along Silom Road and turning down Convent Road. Chong Nonsi BTS station (Silom Line) is just 5 minutes on foot. The hotel has an outdoor pool, G Spa, a 24-hour EnerGy Fitness centre, a G Club Lounge, and four dining outlets including the Michelin Guide-listed Scarlett Wine Bar & Restaurant on the 37th floor. It holds 8.2 out of 10 from 824 real guest reviews on Trip.com and 8.0 on Booking.com from 2,123 reviews. Rates start from approx. ฿2,500/night for a G Deluxe Room.

body.html: For families and carers who need regular access to BNH Hospital — one of Bangkok's most established private hospitals on Convent Road in Silom — finding a comfortable five-star base within walking distance comes down to a short list. Pullman Bangkok Hotel G is the closest 5-star option. Leaving the hotel's main entrance on Silom Road and walking east for about 600 metres, then turning right down Convent Road for another 200 metres, puts you at BNH's main gate in roughly 10 minutes, without needing to book a taxi for every visit. When appointments start early and the Bangkok traffic is unpredictable, that 10-minute walk is genuinely useful.

The hotel sits at 188 Silom Road in a 38-floor tower built in 1992 and last renovated in 2012. Its 469 rooms cover several categories: G Deluxe Rooms on floors 18–25 with white minimalist interiors and floor-to-ceiling windows; G Club Rooms on the 26th floor with Executive Lounge access; Premium Deluxe Rooms on floors 28–31 offering the best city views in the Deluxe category; and G Suites at 77 m² with a separate living area, good for longer stays. Every room includes the Pullman signature pillow menu, complimentary high-speed wired and wireless Wi-Fi, and a deep soaking bathtub in the bathroom.

The hotel's standout dining option is Scarlett Wine Bar & Restaurant on the 37th floor, a French-influenced restaurant that has been listed in the Michelin Guide Bangkok for several years running. The views at night — 360 degrees of Bangkok's skyline — are genuinely spectacular, and the wine list has won multiple International Wine Challenge awards. Downstairs, 25 Degrees Burger Bar runs 24 hours, serving Los Angeles-style burgers to consistently positive reviews; useful for late arrivals and early departures. TIVA Urban Thaittoria offers Thai-Italian fusion, and the Pool Bar on the 5th floor is the low-key choice for a drink by the water. For wellness, EnerGy Fitness operates 24 hours with full Technogym equipment, and G Spa combines Thai healing techniques with modern treatments.

"The location is excellent — Chong Nonsi BTS is literally a 5-minute walk. Scarlett on the 37th floor was a highlight of the whole trip: stunning night views over Bangkok and a wine list that's seriously curated. Staff throughout were warm and handled every request without fuss."

Across Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, real guest reviews repeatedly praise the location near Chong Nonsi BTS, the warmth and professionalism of the staff, and the breadth of the breakfast buffet. Room views from upper floors draw enthusiastic comments, particularly from guests who upgraded to G Club or Premium Deluxe. The 25 Degrees Burger Bar receives consistent love from late-night travellers and early-morning departures alike. Many guests specifically mention the value Scarlett Wine Bar adds to a stay — not every hotel at this price point has a Michelin-listed restaurant on site.

The honest caveats are real and worth knowing before you book. The building dates from 1992 and while it was renovated in 2012, some lower-floor rooms still show their age — a handful of reviews mention dated furnishings, malfunctioning fridges or soap dispensers, and occasional musty odours in rooms below the 20th floor. The outdoor pool is smaller than most photos suggest; it is suited to relaxing rather than serious swimming. During peak hours, elevator wait times can stretch to 10 minutes on busy floors. These issues are consistently reported for lower-category rooms, while upper-floor and G Club bookings receive far fewer complaints.

Overall, Pullman Bangkok Hotel G holds 8.2 out of 10 on Trip.com from 824 real guest reviews and 8.0 on Booking.com from 2,123 reviews. It is a solid pick for anyone needing regular access to BNH Hospital who wants 5-star comfort — the 10-minute walk avoids daily taxi bookings and the hotel's amenities help carers decompress between visits. It also works well for business travellers in the Silom CBD and for couples who want a Michelin-listed rooftop restaurant on their doorstep. Rates start at approx. ฿2,500/night for a G Deluxe Room; the step up to Premium Deluxe or G Club is worth considering given the upgrade in room condition and views.

honestSummary: Pullman Bangkok Hotel G is a strong choice for anyone needing 5-star accommodation within walking distance of BNH Hospital — the location is excellent, the staff are consistently praised, and Scarlett Wine Bar is a genuine draw. The counterweight is a building that dates from 1992: some lower-floor rooms are dated and have maintenance issues. Book a Premium Deluxe or G Club room (floors 26 and above) for the best chance of a smooth stay.
honestChecks: If you want a freshly maintained, up-to-date room — avoid the cheapest G Deluxe rooms on lower floors. Several reviews report dated furnishings and broken in-room items at that tier → book Premium Deluxe (floors 28–31) or G Club to significantly reduce that risk.
If the pool is important to your stay — the outdoor pool is on the small side and is better for unwinding than swimming laps. If pool size matters, compare with other Silom hotels before committing.

If you want G Club Lounge access — it is not included in standard G Deluxe or Deluxe rooms. You need a G Club room booking or a qualifying Accor membership tier → read the room type description carefully before booking to avoid disappointment.

tips.title: Walk to BNH Hospital via Silom Road and Convent Road
tips.body: Leave the main entrance and head east along Silom Road for about 600 metres, then turn right down Convent Road for another 200 metres. BNH Hospital's main entrance is on your left. The whole walk takes around 10 minutes. No major road crossings are needed.

tips.title: Use Chong Nonsi BTS for fast connections
tips.body: Chong Nonsi station (Silom BTS Line) is 5 minutes' walk from the hotel. For the MRT Blue Line, take BTS one stop to Sala Daeng and connect through the covered walkway to Silom MRT — useful for reaching Sukhumvit or the Airport Rail Link.

tips.title: Reserve a table at Scarlett in advance
tips.body: Scarlett Wine Bar & Restaurant on the 37th floor has limited window seats with the best views — these go quickly, especially on Friday and Saturday evenings. Book online through the hotel's website or call directly. Arriving without a reservation on a weekend is a gamble.

tips.title: Choose a higher floor for the best experience
tips.body: The gap between lower and upper floors is unusually large at this hotel. Reviews consistently show that rooms from the 26th floor upward receive fewer complaints and more praise. If budget allows, Premium Deluxe on floors 28–31 is the value sweet spot: better views, better condition, close to Scarlett.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Pullman Bangkok Hotel G

faq.q: How close is Pullman Bangkok Hotel G to BNH Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is at 188 Silom Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok. BNH Hospital (9/1 Convent Road) is approximately 800 metres away — about a 10-minute walk. Head east along Silom Road for roughly 600 metres, then turn right down Convent Road for another 200 metres. BNH's main entrance is on your left. It is the closest 5-star hotel to BNH in the Silom district.

faq.q: How much does Pullman Bangkok Hotel G cost per night?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿2,500/night for a G Deluxe Room (floors 18–25). A G Club Room with Lounge access starts around ฿3,500. Premium Deluxe (floors 28–31) starts around ฿4,200. A G Suite at 77 m² starts around ฿6,500. Prices vary by season and booking platform — always compare across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before confirming.

faq.q: Which BTS or MRT station is closest to Pullman Bangkok Hotel G?
faq.a: Chong Nonsi BTS (Silom Line) is the closest station, just 0.58 km away — about a 5-minute walk. For the MRT Blue Line, the nearest connection is Silom MRT via Sala Daeng BTS (a 10-minute walk or one BTS stop). Sala Daeng connects to Silom MRT through a covered walkway.

faq.q: What facilities does Pullman Bangkok Hotel G have?
faq.a: The hotel has an outdoor pool (5th floor), G Spa, EnerGy Fitness (24 hours, full Technogym equipment), and a G Club Executive Lounge. Dining includes Scarlett Wine Bar & Restaurant on the 37th floor (Michelin Guide Bangkok), 25 Degrees Burger Bar (24 hours), TIVA Urban Thaittoria, and Pool Bar. There are 12 meeting rooms, free wired and wireless Wi-Fi, and airport transfer services.

faq.q: Is Pullman Bangkok Hotel G a good base for a visit to BNH Hospital?
faq.a: Yes, particularly for repeated visits to BNH Hospital. The ~800-metre walking distance means you can walk there without booking a taxi every time. The G Suite (77 m²) has a separate living area that is useful for longer stays. For the most comfortable experience, book a Premium Deluxe or G Club room on the upper floors — lower-floor rooms at this hotel have more mixed reviews.

faq.q: Is Scarlett Wine Bar & Restaurant at Pullman Bangkok Hotel G worth visiting?
faq.a: Yes — Scarlett Wine Bar & Restaurant on the 37th floor has appeared in the Michelin Guide Bangkok for several years. It serves French-influenced food with panoramic Bangkok Skyline views and a wine list that has won International Wine Challenge awards. Window seats fill up quickly, so book a table in advance — especially on Friday and Saturday evenings.
